facts.text: The README describes a Python module that communicates with a Newport 1918 power meter on a Windows computer through ctypes and Newport's usbdll.dll
The module is written for Python 2.7 and the README says it would need minor modifications for Python 3+
The user-facing device class is Newport_1918c
The constructor loads usbdll.dll with windll.LoadLibrary, defaulting to the 32-bit Newport install path and product id 0xCEC7
The constructor opens the device by product id and reads the device id, model number and serial number from get_instrument_list
open_device_with_product_id opens the instrument with newp_usb_open_devices and stores the connection state
get_instrument_list returns the device id, model number and serial number
ask sends a query with newp_usb_send_ascii and reads the reply with newp_usb_get_ascii
write sends a command string with newp_usb_send_ascii
set_wavelength converts a float wavelength to an integer, reads PM:MIN:Lambda? and PM:MAX:Lambda?, and writes PM:Lambda only when the value is inside that range
read_buffer writes the PM:DS:* datastore commands, polls PM:DS:COUNT?, and reads PM:Lambda?, PM:STAT:MEAN? and PM:STAT:SDEV?
read_instant_power sets the wavelength and returns the replies to PM:Lambda? and PM:Power?
close_device closes the instrument with newp_usb_uninit_system
The example measures at a 500 nm wavelength and sweeps 500 to 550 nm with an interval of 10 nm
